Lesson Differentiation Engine

A tool that takes a math or physics objective plus a real student's profile and has Claude generate three genuinely different lessons for it live, each with the learning-science reasoning behind it.

status
prototype
section
lab
built with
Claude API, JavaScript
source code →

## problem

Some students can't be reached by a lesson written for “the average student”, and differentiation is the answer — but writing one genuinely different version of a lesson, grounded in real learning science, can take longer than writing the original. Most teachers end up differentiating by instinct, without the bandwidth to do it well for more than one or two students at a time.

## solution

Give the engine a real math or physics objective and a student profile, and Claude generates three structurally different instructional pathways live — each with a margin note explaining why it fits that student, grounded in executive-function and UDL research. The teacher still picks, adapts and knows the kid; the tool does the first draft of the reasoning.

## details

  • The interface is drawn like a technical blueprint, because a lesson plan is an engineering problem: a fixed objective, real constraints, and a structure that gets from one to the other.
  • Next ideas: saving and editing pathways into a lesson library, a “why not” mode that names the approaches it avoided, and batching several students for one class period.
